speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) whether there are any plans to strengthen the regulatory regime for nursing homes to ensure that systemic lapses similar to those identified at the Windsor Convalescent Home do not recur at any other nursing home; and (b) if not, why not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Such an approach ensures that shortcomings and lapses in nursing homes are addressed and rectified in a timely way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In response to previous identified non-compliances, MOH conducted a thematic audit focusing on compliance with infection prevention and control practices, and basic custodial and nursing care for selected higher-risk operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: After the gaps were first identified, operators were given an opportunity to rectify the lapses, during which we intensified our monitoring of and engagement with the operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: MOH and the Agency for Integrated Care will also be sharing the findings of our recent audits, and the various manpower training and grant support available with the nursing home sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will help the sector maintain an appropriate standard of care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In response to Mr Fadli Fawzi, like all regulatory functions, it is impossible to eradicate and prevent recurrences of lapses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But with a robust regime, we can uphold good standards of operations and constructive relationships between the regulator and operator to better serve the residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Lee Hong Chuang asked about claims and compensation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: MOH's regulatory framework aims at assessing licensees' care delivery practices and protocols in compliance with the Healthcare Services Act to ensure resident safety.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
text: My second question is, will MOH consider providing smaller nursing home operators with greater support, for example, through a review of foreign manpower requirements?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The audit findings for these two nursing homes are a feature, not a bug of our regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As mentioned earlier in my reply, a large majority of these nursing homes with identified areas of improvement have taken steps to rectify them and sustain the improvements over time.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In cases where we believe that they have not done so after repeated engagements with them, we take the extreme step of revoking licence and making sure that we take care of the residents who are in their care.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: To his point about supporting nursing homes, we do support our nursing homes through different support from manpower training grants to other support for nursing homes, raising the collective standard of care and professionalism across the whole nursing home sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, this is something we have been doing and will continue to do.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: If things really do not improve, then we take the extreme step of engaging licence operators.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In these two cases of nursing homes, we had to revoke their licence and make arrangements for residents to be get taken called of in another facility.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are the primary objectives, but we will continue to see how we can think about meaningful information for family members.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I know family members when they put their loved ones in nursing homes, there is a range of factors they consider.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: First and foremost will be the safety, the health and welfare of the resident in the nursing home, but other factors include affordability, include different kind of considerations like vicinity to their home and so on.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: There are different and a myriad of variables in terms of consideration.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: MOH is continually looking at how we can provide meaningful information for caregivers and family members to make a decision.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think I will squeeze in one last Parliamentary Question.
